brokers.name: Arrests.org
brokers.opt_out_email: <verify: removal contact email is Cloudflare-email-protected on third-party guides, literal address not independently confirmed>
brokers.notes: WebFetch of arrests.org returned HTTP 403 (site live, actively bot-blocking). Multiple independent 2025-2026 removal guides (Incogni, Onerep, PurePrivacy, idstrong, EXPOSE, mugshotremovalservice) converge on the same mechanism: a mugshot/arrest-record aggregator organized by state; removal via a per-listing form at arrests.org/remove/?id=<RecordID> (Record ID taken from your listing's URL), where you select a removal reason (charges dropped/not adjudicated guilty, sealed/expunged, or 'remove my date of birth and address') and upload a redacted government photo ID (name/DOB/photo visible, other fields blacked out) plus supporting court documentation if applicable. An alternate email-based route is described by multiple guides but the literal address is Cloudflare-email-protected in every source found and could not be confirmed -- left as a <verify:> placeholder rather than guessed. Guides consistently state removal itself is free ('Arrests.org doesn't charge for it, but it does require photo ID verification'), but also consistently warn that paid 'expedited removal' resellers have historically marked up what should be a free process -- charges_fee left false per the site's own stated policy, with a strong do-not-pay warning in the instructions below. Processing 5-30 days. gov_id + guided tier reflect the photo-ID upload requirement; legal_basis left [none] since no CCPA/GDPR opt-out-of-sale framing was found -- this is a direct takedown-request process, not a statutory data-sale opt-out. last_verified left null.
brokers.instructions_md:
1. Find your listing on arrests.org and copy the Record ID from its URL.
2. Go to the removal form, following the pattern https://arrests.org/remove/?id=<your Record ID> (replace with the ID from step 1).
3. Select the removal reason that applies to you: charges were dropped/not adjudicated guilty, the arrest was sealed or expunged, or you're only requesting removal of your date of birth and address from the listing.
4. Upload a redacted copy of a government-issued photo ID -- black out everything except your name, date of birth, and photo -- plus any supporting court documents (expungement order, disposition record) relevant to your selected reason.
5. Submit the form and allow 5-30 days for a decision; Arrests.org does not always grant removal requests and may not remove all associated data even when it does.
6. Do not pay anyone for "expedited" removal -- legitimate removal through Arrests.org's own process is free, and paid resellers offering faster removal have been reported as a markup scheme, not an official service.
7. Removing the listing here is a privacy/visibility fix only -- the underlying arrest record remains in official court and police databases until you separately expunge or seal it through the court system.

**Sensitive-data note:** this process requires uploading a (redacted) government photo ID. Only proceed if you're comfortable sharing that; there's no lower-friction alternative documented.

Background-check broker reselling records on named individuals -> people_search true, crucial priority.
brokers.instructions_md:
1. Email info@backgroundchecks.com stating you are exercising your CCPA right to opt out of the sale/sharing of your personal information (and/or requesting deletion).
2. In the same email, include: your full name, every physical address associated with your record, every email address on file, every phone number on file, and every employer listed.
3. Attach a legible image of a government-issued ID showing your California address -- Backgroundchecks.com requires this to verify your identity before acting on the request.
4. If your concern is about the accuracy of an FCRA background-check report rather than a CCPA sale opt-out, use their disputes page at backgroundchecks.com/disputes instead, which follows FCRA dispute procedures.
5. Keep a copy of your email and ID submission for your records, and follow up if you don't receive confirmation within a reasonable time.

brokers.name: BustedMugshots.com
brokers.opt_out_url: <verify: locate the current removal-policy/FAQ page on bustedmugshots.com -- not reliably reachable via automated fetch (TLS errors)>
brokers.notes: BustedMugshots.com aggregates and publishes arrest-record mugshots and is a well-documented mugshot-broker site. Multiple independent opt-out guides (Comparitech, DeleteMe, Incogni, InternetPrivacy) consistently describe the same narrow removal path: the site states it does not accept payment for removal and is not currently processing general removal requests, but will remove listings for cases that were sealed, expunged, resulted in acquittal/dismissal, or where the subject is deceased -- if the requester supplies supporting court/legal documentation via help@bustedmugshots.com. This is a documentation-gated process (not a plain opt-out), so classified tier:guided despite method:email, and id_required:true because court/legal documents (functionally government-issued proof) are required. Direct WebFetch of bustedmugshots.com pages failed with TLS/certificate errors during research, so this is reconstructed from third-party guides rather than a freshly rendered page; opt_out_url left as a verify placeholder and last_verified is null.
brokers.instructions_md:
1. Determine whether your case qualifies: BustedMugshots.com states it will only remove listings where the case was sealed, expunged, you were found not guilty, the charges were dismissed, or the subject is deceased. It does not offer general removal and does not accept payment for removal.
2. Gather supporting documentation proving your case qualifies -- e.g. a court order of expungement/sealing, a dismissal record, or (for a deceased subject) a certified death certificate.
3. Email help@bustedmugshots.com with your full name, a link to your specific listing on the site, and the supporting documentation attached.
4. Keep your request factual, polite, and non-threatening -- removal in qualifying cases is reportedly handled at the site's discretion.
5. If your case does not meet one of these narrow criteria, BustedMugshots.com is unlikely to remove your listing directly; consider a broader reputation-management/suppression strategy instead.
6. Because BustedMugshots.com is only one of many mugshot-aggregator sites, a successful removal here will not remove copies of the same mugshot from other, separately operated mugshot sites -- each requires its own request.

brokers.name: California Brokers (licensedata.org network)
brokers.notes: californiabrokers.org is NOT a state licensing board -- it is an independent, unofficial directory that republishes California real estate broker license records (name, license status/number, renewal dates) with a search/browse UI and user reviews. It is one of a confirmed family of near-identical sites (californiabrokers.org, californiaengineering.org, californialicensing.org, californianursing.org, californiapharmacists.org, plus others referenced in their shared footer such as 'California Contractors' and 'California Dentists') that cross-link each other and share the exact same removal/contact infrastructure. Confirmed via WebFetch of each site's /contact page: all use Cloudflare email-obfuscation resolving to removals@licensedata.org and contact@licensedata.org (decoded the cloudflare cdn-cgi/l/email-protection hex payloads directly), establishing a single common operator running under the licensedata.org backend. The site explicitly discourages delisting ('doing so will prevent others from verifying your license') but does process removal-by-email requests, identified by a per-record ID shown on each license listing. Since it publishes business/professional license info (not home addresses) with a working, direct-email opt-out and no CAPTCHA/ID gate described -> tier:auto, method:email. people_search left false (this is a professional-license registry, not a general identity/address lookup), but priority:high given it publishes named individuals' license records publicly with reviews and only a narrow, easy-to-miss removal path. opt_out_url left null because the removal flow requires locating your own listing's page (which contains a per-record ID) rather than a fixed opt-out landing page.
brokers.instructions_md:
1. Go to https://www.californiabrokers.org/ and search for your own name to find your license listing.
2. Open your listing and note the record ID shown in the bottom-right corner of the license-details block -- you'll need this for the removal request.
3. Email removals@licensedata.org and include the record ID plus your full name as it appears on the listing, asking that your record be removed from californiabrokers.org.
4. Note that the site explicitly warns that removing your listing may make it harder for others to verify your license through this particular (unofficial) site -- your official license status remains verifiable through the California Department of Real Estate regardless.
5. Because this site is part of a shared network (californiaengineering.org, californialicensing.org, californianursing.org, californiapharmacists.org, and others) run by the same operator, a removal request to removals@licensedata.org may need to be repeated separately for each site where your license type has its own listing -- check the related sites linked in the footer if you hold multiple licenses.

brokers.name: OptOutPrescreen.com
brokers.notes: IMPORTANT: this is NOT a data broker to remove yourself from -- it is the official, FTC/FCRA-mandated Consumer Credit Reporting Industry opt-out portal, operated jointly by the four nationwide credit bureaus (Equifax, Experian, Innovis, and TransUnion) under the Fair Credit Reporting Act and FACTA. It exists so consumers CAN stop receiving prescreened ('pre-approved') credit and insurance offers -- it does not sell or expose your data, and using it reduces junk mail/solicitation exposure rather than creating any. Included here because it's a legitimate, high-value consumer self-help tool adjacent to this project's mission, not because it's a broker in the usual sense. Direct WebFetch of the homepage returned HTTP 403 (bot-blocked) in this session, so last_verified is left null; corroborated instead via Wikipedia's OptOutPrescreen.com article and multiple credit-bureau/consumer sources (TransUnion, Experian, Equifax, FTC consumer.ftc.gov, Cybernews) which are consistent on the mechanics. The online 5-year opt-out asks for name, address, DOB, and SSN (used only to match you against bureau prescreening lists, per the site's stated purpose) -- required_fields reflects the online option; the permanent opt-out avoids submitting SSN online by instead mailing a signed paper form. priority set to high (not crucial, per instructions) since this is a consumer-empowerment tool rather than an exposure to remediate. Beware impostor sites/calls: the real service will not call or email you first.
brokers.instructions_md:
1. Go to the official site at [optoutprescreen.com](https://www.optoutprescreen.com/) -- verify the URL carefully, as scam sites mimic this domain, and note the real service never calls or emails you first.
2. Choose to opt out (rather than opt in) of prescreened credit and insurance offers.
3. For the quick 5-year electronic opt-out, submit your name, address, date of birth, and Social Security number online (this data is used only to match you against the credit bureaus' prescreening lists) -- or call 1-888-567-8688 (1-888-5-OPTOUT) to do the same by phone.
4. If you want a permanent opt-out instead of the 5-year term, start the request online or by phone, then print, sign, and mail in the confirmation form the site provides -- permanent opt-out cannot be completed electronically alone.
5. There is no fee either way; this stops prescreened offers, not all marketing mail, so pair it with DMAchoice if you also want to cut down on general marketing mail.
6. The 5-year opt-out will lapse -- if you chose that option, calendar a reminder to renew, or just do the permanent mail-in version once to avoid repeating this.

brokers.name: AmRent
brokers.notes: WebFetched amrent.com/privacy and amrent.com/consumer_assistance directly; both loaded and confirmed the process described below. AmRent is a tenant/resident-screening consumer reporting agency (used by landlords, integrated into Rent Manager and similar property-management software), not a classic address/people-search broker despite the legacy CSV's 'People Search' tag. Its own privacy notice states it is exempt from CCPA-style opt-out because it is a consumer reporting agency governed by FCRA/GLBA instead -- 'If you submit your request to us, we may deny the request' for requests that should go to the landlord/data controller. There is no 'opt out of sale' mechanism; the only real consumer-facing rights are FCRA file access and dispute, via phone, mail, or downloadable Consumer Dispute Form / Request My Report Form (no online portal, no email intake -- email is explicitly discouraged). No fee. No government ID required for a standard report/dispute request (ID is only required for the separate human-trafficking-block process). Because the actual lever available to consumers is dispute/access rather than removal, and the site is FCRA-exempt from CCPA, priority is standard rather than crucial; tier is guided because it's phone/mail/form-only with no self-service portal.
brokers.instructions_md:

If you were denied housing or want to see what's in your AmRent tenant-screening report, request your free copy by mail or fax: download the "Request My Report Form" from [amrent.com/privacy](http://www.amrent.com/privacy) or [amrent.com/consumer_assistance](http://www.amrent.com/consumer_assistance), fill it out, and mail it to AmRent Consumer Assistance, PO Box 530091, Atlanta, GA 30353 (or call to ask about faxing it).
